\[PROPOSED\] additions (no new public lifecycle hooks):

**Token map and transforms**

- `RunContext.anonymization` slot in `…/agent-builder-server/runner/runner.ts`.

- An `AnonymizingChatModel` decorator class (lives in `kbn-anonymization`) that wraps any `InferenceChatModel` from `@kbn/inference-langchain` with transform-out (forward map applied before `invoke()`) and transform-in (inverse map applied on the response stream). AB instantiates one per round and substitutes it for the inner model at the five call sites (researcher, answer agent, structured answer, title generation, conversation compaction). Other plugins compose the decorator the same way at construction time.

- Transform-in gating on event type:

  - **Natural-language chunks** (`messageChunk` / `messageComplete` / `reasoning`) → deanonymize for client emission.

  - **Tool-call event params** → deanonymize for the **client/storage path** (recursive `Map.get` on string-leaf values); keep the LLM-context copy tokenized for `beforeToolCall` (§3.4).

  - `thinkingComplete` is excluded \- no text payload.

- System prompt instruction injection in transform-out (§3.7) \- AB-owned, no user configuration required. Generated dynamically from the round's `entities` set; cost noted in §6.6.

**`beforeAgent` integration**

- Token map merge logic in the `beforeAgent` hook handler (§3.6) \- unions maps from all configured workflows in the per-round ID list; aborts the round on same-source-different-class collision.

- Extension of `BeforeAgentWorkflowOutput` (`hooks/agent_workflows/types.ts:14-18`) with `forward`, `inverse`, `entities`, `toolDeanonymization` fields, plus the read path in `runBeforeAgentWorkflows` to populate `RunContext.anonymization`.

- Extension of `workflowParams` shape passed by `runBeforeAgentWorkflows` to include a synthesized `event: { message, conversationSalt, agentId, … }` object. **`message` is the new user message concatenated with the textual content of the round's outgoing LLM context** (per §4.1's history-inclusion policy: detection window \= LLM-visible window, by construction). `runWorkflow` already destructures `event` onto `context.event`, so YAML `{{ event.X }}` resolves correctly.

**Latency fast-path (§4.4)**

- Parameterize `executeWorkflow`'s polling cadence: add `initialWaitMs` and `checkIntervalMs` overrides (current defaults `1000` / `2500` stay for general callers). AB's anonymization invocation passes `{ initialWaitMs: 0, checkIntervalMs: 50 }`. \~10-line change in `execute_workflow.ts` and `run_before_agent_workflows.ts`.

- Single-step bypass in `runBeforeAgentWorkflows`: inspect the workflow definition; if it contains exactly one operative step and that step is `ai.pii`, extract the step config and run the step factory directly via `createAiPiiStepDefinition` instead of invoking the engine. Multi-step workflows fall back to the engine path with parameterized polling.

- Telemetry parity: the bypass path emits the same span/event shape that the engine path emits, so observability dashboards see uniform data regardless of which path ran.

- (Future) engine-side completion notification: a Promise/event-based completion signal in the workflows engine eliminates polling entirely. AB adopts it invisibly when it lands; the call-site contract here doesn't change. Out of scope for this RFC.

**Tool hooks**

- `beforeToolCall` blocking hook: deanonymize tool params for allowlisted tools (§3.4 step 1–4).  
- `afterToolCall` blocking hook: **run `ai.pii` detection on tool result text first**, extend `forward`/`inverse` with newly-detected entities, then re-anonymize results (§3.4). Closes the within-round new-PII leak.

**`kbn-anonymization` package**

- `ai.pii` and `transform.pii_restore` step definitions, registered through factory functions that return a `BaseStepDefinition` from `@kbn/workflows` (same shape as `ai.classify` et al.):

  - `createAiPiiStepDefinition({ regexExecutor, … }): BaseStepDefinition` \- supplies `id: 'ai.pii'`, `category: StepCategory.Ai`, `label`/`description`/`documentation` (i18n), and Zod `inputSchema` / `outputSchema` / `configSchema`. The schemas drive the editor's form rendering (§2.1 step 1\) and runtime validation; in particular `inputSchema` enumerates `entities` from `ANONYMIZATION_ENTITY_CLASSES`, validates `regex_rules` (compile \+ class-membership at save time, §4.2), and accepts an optional `system_prompt_instruction` override (§3.7).

  - `createTransformPiiRestoreStepDefinition(): BaseStepDefinition` \- analogous, for ad-hoc deanonymization inside non-AB workflows (§4.1).

  - `createRegexWorkerPool(opts: { size, timeoutMs }): RegexExecutor` \- Piscina pool factory; importing plugin owns lifecycle (§4.2).

- User-authored patterns from `regex_rules` execute on the same Piscina worker pool as bundled rules and flow through the same `resolve_overlaps_and_mask` layer (§4.2).

- Re-declarations (since `anonymization-common` is being deleted): `NER_MODEL_ID`, `NER_ENTITY_CLASSES`, `ANONYMIZATION_ENTITY_CLASSES`, `generateToken`.

- The `AnonymizingChatModel` decorator class.

**Persistence**

- A `salt: string` field on AB's conversation Elasticsearch document mapping (`ConversationService` persistence; not a SavedObject) per §6.2.

**Trust boundary enforcement (§4.2)**

- Runtime guard in the step executor (load-bearing): resolves `ner_deployment_id` against the ML trained models registry; defence-in-depth rejects any value that resolves to an `_inference` endpoint with `task_type: chat_completion`.

- Best-effort static check at workflow registration: warns on `ner_deployment_id` matching an LLM connector ID at the time of registration.

**CI guard against direct `inference.chatComplete` calls (§3.2)**

- Either an ESLint rule scoped to `agent_builder/server/**` that flags `inference.chatComplete(` and `inference.outputs.complete(` outside an explicit allowlist, *or* a typed wrapper in `agent-builder-server` that is the only sanctioned export and the underlying contract is not re-exported. Without one of these, a future contributor adding a direct call would silently bypass anonymization. Cheap insurance.
